mainTopic: Hearing part of a שופר blast, blowing a שופר that is forbidden for benefit, the rule מצוות לאו ליהנות ניתנו, and doing a מצוה without intention.
overview: רבה rules that a שופר blast heard partly in a pit and partly at its edge counts, but one heard partly before dawn and partly after dawn does not. The גמרא defends the difference: night is never a time for the מצוה, while a pit is a valid place for those inside it. After testing whether part of a blast is enough, the גמרא concludes that it is not, and explains that רבה meant a blower climbing out of the pit who hears the whole blast himself. רב יהודה then rules on a שופר from an עולה or from שלמים. רבא first says neither works and then rules that both work, because מצוות לאו ליהנות ניתנו. רב יהודה adds that a שופר of עבודה זרה works after the fact, but one from an עיר הנדחת does not, since its size counts as already crushed. רבא applies his principle to vows against benefit, unless the מצוה also brings physical pleasure. Finally, from the ruling that one forced to eat מצה is יצא, רבא learns that one who blows שופר for music is יצא, and the גמרא begins explaining why this needed to be said, continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: רבה's two rulings: pit and edge counts, before and after dawn does not
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that a blast heard partly in the pit and partly at its edge is valid. A blast heard partly before dawn and partly after dawn is not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone heard part of the blast in the pit and part of it at the edge of the pit, he has fulfilled his obligation. If he heard part of the blast before dawn and part after dawn, he has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives two rulings about a single תקיעה that is split between two situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases only part of the blast was heard in a fully valid way. Yet רבה treats the cases differently: the pit-and-edge blast counts, while the before-and-after-dawn blast does not. The rest of this section tries to explain that difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Dawn (literally, the pillar of the dawn), when the day's מצוה time begins

steps.whyThisMatters: These two rulings are the base that אביי challenges and the גמרא later draws inferences from.

phrases.english: If one heard part of the blast in the pit

phrases.aramaic: וּמִקְצָת תְּקִיעָה עַל שְׂפַת הַבּוֹר — יָצָא.
phrases.english: and part of the blast at the edge of the pit, he has fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.aramaic: מִקְצָת תְּקִיעָה קוֹדֶם שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר
phrases.english: If he heard part of the blast before dawn rose

phrases.aramaic: וּמִקְצָת תְּקִיעָה לְאַחַר שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: and part of the blast after dawn rose, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבה's statement from the previous part of the sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Part in the pit and part at the edge counts. Part before dawn and part after dawn does not.

steps.title: אביי asks why the two cases are different
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the reason the dawn case fails should make the pit case fail too.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: What is different there? There, the whole blast must be heard at a time of obligation, and it was not. Here too, the whole blast must be heard in a place of obligation, and it was not!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה, saying the two rulings should come out the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumes the dawn case fails because the whole blast must be valid from beginning to end. If that is the rule, the pit case should fail too, since part of that blast was heard in a place that does not work. So רבה's two rulings seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: In a state of obligation, meaning a time or place where the מצוה can be done

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבה, who gave the rulings in step 1.

phrases.english: What is different there?
That we need the whole blast in a time of obligation, and it is not so.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי — בָּעֵינָא כּוּלַּהּ תְּקִיעָה בְּחִיּוּבָא, וְלֵיכָּא!
phrases.english: Here too we need the whole blast in a place of obligation, and it is not so!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מַאי שְׁנָא הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the difference רבה drew between his two rulings.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that the pit-and-edge blast counts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the whole blast must be valid in the dawn case, the same requirement should disqualify the pit case.

steps.title: Night is never valid, but a pit is valid for those inside it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that night is not a time for the מצוה at all, while a pit is a valid place for the people standing in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, night is not a time of obligation at all. Here, a pit is a place of obligation for the people standing in the pit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי and defends רבה by showing the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The part of the blast heard at night has no value at all, because night is never a time for שופר. The part heard in the pit is a real תקיעה for anyone standing inside the pit. Its problem is only a matter of the situation, not a basic flaw, so it can join with the part heard at the edge.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? It is not the same at all!

steps.whatToRemember: A part of the blast that is valid for someone (the pit) can join with the rest. A part that is not valid for anyone (night) cannot.

phrases.english: How can you compare them?!

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם — לַיְלָה לָאו זְמַן חִיּוּבָא הוּא כְּלָל,
phrases.english: There, night is not a time of obligation at all,
here, a pit is a place of obligation
for those standing in the pit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought both cases fail because the whole blast must be valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Night is not valid for anyone, but a pit is valid for some people, so the pit portion can join with the rest of the blast.

steps.title: Does רבה hold that only the end, or only the beginning, is enough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבה's pit ruling means that hearing only the end of a blast counts, and so also only the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that רבה holds that if someone heard the end of a blast without its beginning, he has fulfilled his obligation? And it follows on its own that if he heard the beginning without the end, he has also fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a possible conclusion from רבה's ruling and asks whether he really means it. This sets up the next part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the part heard in the pit does not count for the listener, then he really heard only the end of the blast, and רבה still says he fulfilled his obligation. That would mean the end alone is enough. By the same reasoning, the beginning alone should be enough too. The גמרא is checking whether רבה truly holds this.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a question, not רבה's actual ruling. The גמרא is testing what his pit ruling would imply.

phrases.english: Is this to say that Rabba holds:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁמַע סוֹף תְּקִיעָה בְּלֹא תְּחִילַּת תְּקִיעָה — יָצָא,
phrases.english: If one heard the end of a blast without the beginning of the blast, he has fulfilled his obligation,
and it follows automatically:

phrases.aramaic: תְּחִילַּת תְּקִיעָה בְּלֹא סוֹף תְּקִיעָה — יָצָא.
phrases.english: if he heard the beginning of a blast without the end of the blast, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication from רבה's pit ruling, now that it has been defended.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבה holds that hearing only part of a blast, either the end or the beginning, is enough to fulfill the obligation.

steps.title: Proof attempt from the stretched blast
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: if someone stretches one תקיעה to the length of two, it counts as only one. If part of a blast counted, why shouldn't it count as two?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if someone blew the first תקיעה, then stretched the second one as long as two, he only gets credit for one. But why? Let it count as two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from step 4 using a משנה. That משנה seems to show that part of a blast does not count as a blast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If half a blast counted, the first half of the long blast could serve as the end of one set and the second half as the start of the next set. Since the משנה gives credit for only one, it looks like part of a blast is worth nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: He stretched out (made the blast longer)
Let it count for him as two

phrases.english: Come and hear: if one blew the first [blast],
and stretched the second as long as two,
phrases.notes: The "second" is the closing תקיעה of the first set. He hoped it would also open the next set.

phrases.english: he only has one [to his credit].
But why? Let it count for him as two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle step 4's question from a משנה
steps.raayaObject: Part of a blast does not count as a blast
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about stretching the second תקיעה to the length of two

steps.title: We never split one blast into two
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed aside: the reason it counts as one is that one blast is never divided into two. It has nothing to do with whether part of a blast counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not cut blasts apart from each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 5. It gives a different reason for that משנה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if hearing part of a blast is enough, one continuous blast cannot be split and counted twice. So the משנה does not tell us anything about our question.

phrases.english: We do not cut blasts apart from each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 5's proof
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the stretched-blast משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's ruling comes from a separate rule (no splitting one blast), not from whether part of a blast counts

steps.title: Proof from blowing into a pit
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that someone who hears only the echo from a pit is not יצא. If part of a blast counted, he should be יצא with the clear beginning, before the echo mixes in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if someone blows into a pit, a cistern, or a large jug, if he heard the שופר's sound he is יצא; if he heard an echo, he is not יצא. But why? Let him be יצא with the start of the blast, before the sound gets mixed up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second משנה. This one really does show that part of a blast is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every blast into a pit starts clear, and only then does the echo mix in. If hearing the clear beginning were enough, nobody would ever fail here. Since the משנה says he can fail, part of a blast does not count, and that seems to go against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A cistern (a large pit for water)
An echo, a hollow mixed-up sound

phrases.english: Come and hear: one who blows into a pit

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַדּוּת אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַפִּיטָס,
phrases.english: or into a cistern or into a large jug,
if he heard the sound of the שופר, he is יצא;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם קוֹל הֲבָרָה שָׁמַע — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: and if he heard the sound of an echo, he is not יצא.
But why? Let him be יצא with the beginning of the blast,
before the sound gets mixed up!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 6 pushes aside the first proof, the גמרא brings a stronger one
steps.raayaObject: Part of a blast does not count, which seems to go against רבה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about blowing into a pit, cistern, or jug
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication from step 4 that רבה holds hearing part of a blast is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every blast into a pit begins clear before the echo mixes in. If part of a blast counted, no one could ever fail there, yet the משנה says one who hears an echo is not יצא.

steps.title: רבה meant the blower himself climbing out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that part of a blast does not count. It rereads רבה as talking about a person blowing for himself while climbing out of the pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבה said it, he meant someone who blows and climbs up for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves רבה's ruling by giving it a new meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה is no longer talking about listeners who caught only part of the blast. The blower stays right next to the שופר the whole time, so he hears the entire blast clearly. Part of the blast is in the pit and part at the edge, but he hears all of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Blows and climbs up at the same time

steps.confusionAlert: The question from step 4 is now answered: hearing only part of a blast does NOT count. רבה's ruling stays valid only because the blower heard the whole blast.

phrases.english: When רבה said it,
it was about one who blows and climbs up for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem step 7 raised for רבה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the earlier ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה was talking about listeners who heard only part of the blast
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה was talking about the blower himself, who heard the whole blast

steps.title: Then why did רבה need to say it?
steps.stepSummary: If רבה only meant the blower who heard everything, his ruling seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from step 8: under it, רבה's ruling looks pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who heard a full, clear blast is obviously יצא. So why would רבה bother teaching it?

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (It is obvious)

phrases.english: If so, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading given in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The new reading of רבה from step 8
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading the ruling is obvious, so there was no reason to state it

steps.title: His head may come out before the שופר
steps.stepSummary: רבה needed to say it, because you might worry that the blower's head comes out while the שופר is still inside, so he hears a mixed sound. רבה teaches that he is still יצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: sometimes he gets his head out while the שופר is still in the pit, and the sound gets mixed up. So רבה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 9 by showing a real reason to worry. That worry is what makes רבה's ruling worth saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While climbing out, the blower's ears might be outside the pit while the שופר is still inside. Then he might hear an echo-like sound. רבה teaches that we don't worry about this, and the blower is יצא.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (that the worry is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: Hearing only part of a שופר blast does not count. רבה's pit ruling is about a blower climbing out who hears the whole blast himself. We don't worry that his head comes out before the שופר.

phrases.english: You might have said: sometimes he gets his head out
while the שופר is still in the pit,
and the sound gets mixed up;
so it teaches us [otherwise].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a real worry that the ruling removes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His head might come out before the שופר, so he would hear a mixed sound and not be יצא
steps.terutzMaskana: We don't worry about that, and he is יצא

steps.title: A שופר from an עולה versus from שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says you should not blow a שופר from an עולה or from שלמים. After the fact, with an עולה you are יצא, but with שלמים you are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: With a שופר of an עולה, one should not blow, but if he did blow, he is יצא. With a שופר of שלמים, one should not blow, and if he did blow, he is not יצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ruling from רב יהודה about a שופר that belongs to a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both animals are holy, so using either horn is forbidden from the start. But רב יהודה gives a different result after the fact: עולה works, שלמים does not. The next steps will explain why the two are different.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt-offering, a קרבן that is completely holy
Peace-offerings, a קרבן of lesser holiness
From the start / after the fact (the 'should not blow' versus 'if he blew' pattern)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
With the shofar of a burnt-offering,
one should not blow;
but if he blew, he has fulfilled his obligation.
With the shofar of a peace-offering,
one should not blow;
and if he blew, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of blowing in a pit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שופר of an עולה: not to be used, but if used he is יצא. שופר of שלמים: not to be used, and if used he is not יצא.

steps.title: Why the difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why עולה and שלמים have different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב יהודה's split ruling. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both horns come from holy animals, so it is not obvious why one works and the other does not. The question asks what makes them different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רב יהודה's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why an עולה שופר works after the fact but a שלמים שופר does not.

steps.title: The answer: מעילה makes the עולה non-holy
steps.stepSummary: Misusing an עולה counts as מעילה, which takes it out of holiness, so the horn becomes regular. שלמים are not subject to מעילה, so the prohibition stays on them and they never become regular.
steps.simpleTranslation: An עולה is subject to מעילה. Once he misuses it, it leaves its holiness and becomes regular. שלמים are not subject to מעילה, so the prohibition stays attached to them, and they do not become regular.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב יהודה: misusing an עולה takes it out of holiness, but misusing שלמים does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that when someone commits מעילה with a holy item, it loses its holiness. Blowing with the עולה's horn is מעילה, so the horn becomes regular and he is יצא. שלמים are not covered by מעילה at this stage, so the horn stays forbidden and he is not יצא.

keyTerms.meaning: Misusing holy property for personal use

phrases.english: A burnt-offering is subject to misuse of holy property;
once he has misused it,
it goes out to become non-holy.
Peace-offerings, which are not subject to misuse,
a prohibition rests on them,
and they do not go out to become non-holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מעילה takes an עולה out to חולין, so its horn is usable after the fact. שלמים are not subject to מעילה, so they stay forbidden.

steps.title: רבא: The misuse only happens after the blowing
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects: the מעילה only takes place once the blowing is done. So while he is blowing, the עולה horn is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged this: When does he commit מעילה? After he has blown. So while he is blowing, he is blowing with something forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the explanation from step 13 by pointing out the timing of the מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The horn only becomes regular through the act of blowing, so the change happens at the end. During the blowing itself the horn is still holy and forbidden. That means the עולה should be no better than the שלמים.

phrases.english: Rava strongly objected to this:
When does he commit misuse?
After he has blown.
While he is blowing,
he is blowing with something forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that מעילה makes the עולה שופר valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The horn only becomes חולין after the blowing is complete, so the blowing itself was done with a forbidden horn.

steps.title: רבא's first ruling: neither one works
steps.stepSummary: Because of his challenge, רבא rules that with both the עולה שופר and the שלמים שופר, the person is not יצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Both this one and that one, he is not יצא.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רב יהודה's reasoning, רבא gives his own ruling: neither שופר works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the מעילה explanation falls apart, nothing sets the עולה apart from the שלמים. So רבא treats both the same way, and in both he is not יצא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the earlier view and giving a new one)
Both this one and that one

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: Both this one and that one, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from רבא's challenge and replaces רב יהודה's split ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שופר of an עולה and of שלמים: in both cases he is not יצא.

steps.title: רבא changes his mind: both work
steps.stepSummary: רבא reverses himself and rules that the person is יצא with both, because doing a מצוה is not counted as personal benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he said again: Both this one and that one, he is יצא. מצוות were not given for personal benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes back his first ruling and says the person is יצא with either shofar. He gives the principle מצוות לאו ליהנות ניתנו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on using holy property is a ban on getting personal benefit from it. Fulfilling a מצוה is not counted as personal benefit. So blowing for the מצוה is not forbidden use of the horn, and he is יצא with both.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said again (changing his mind)
מצוות were not given for personal benefit

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's final view: a שופר from either an עולה or שלמים still works after the fact, because מצוות לאו ליהנות ניתנו. Doing a מצוה does not count as benefiting from the holy item.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying you may blow with a holy horn from the start. This step only addresses whether you are יצא if you already blew.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle מצוות לאו ליהנות ניתנו is a basic rule that appears in many places across ש"ס.

phrases.english: He then said:
phrases.notes: רבא is reversing the ruling he just gave.

phrases.english: Both this one and that one, he has fulfilled his obligation.
מצוות were not given for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses רבא's ruling from step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: With a שופר of either an עולה or שלמים, he is יצא after the fact, because מצוות לאו ליהנות ניתנו.

steps.title: רב יהודה on a שופר of עבודה זרה and of an עיר הנדחת
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a שופר of עבודה זרה should not be used, but if it was, the person is יצא. A שופר of an עיר הנדחת should not be used, and if it was, the person is not יצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Don't blow a שופר that was used for עבודה זרה, but if you did, you fulfilled the מצוה. Don't blow a שופר from an עיר הנדחת, a city that was led into עבודה זרה, and if you did, you did not fulfill the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives two rulings about blowing a שופר that is forbidden for benefit. The two cases end up with different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases you should not blow in the first place. But after the fact, the person is יצא with the עבודה זרה שופר and not יצא with the עיר הנדחת שופר. The גמרא explains only the second ruling, in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Idol worship; here, a שופר that was used for it
A Jewish city most of whose people worshipped idols; the תורה says it and its property must be burned
He should not blow (in the first place)
But if he did blow (after the fact)

steps.confusionAlert: Both שופרות are forbidden to use in the first place. The difference is only what happens after the fact: יצא with the עבודה זרה שופר, not יצא with the עיר הנדחת שופר.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
With a shofar of idol worship,
one should not blow, but if he did blow, he fulfilled his obligation.
With a shofar of a city led astray into idol worship,
phrases.notes: This is the city in דברים 13 whose people turned to idols. Everything in it has to be burned.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִתְקַע, וְאִם תָּקַע — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: one should not blow, and if he did blow, he did not fulfill his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: בְּשׁוֹפָר שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling by רב יהודה on another pair of forbidden shofars, following his earlier ruling about עולה and שלמים in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שופר of עבודה זרה: not to be used in the first place, but יצא after the fact. A שופר of an עיר הנדחת: not to be used, and not יצא even after the fact.

steps.title: Why the עיר הנדחת שופר does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a שופר from an עיר הנדחת does not work even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the second ruling. This short question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both שופרות are forbidden, yet only the עיר הנדחת שופר fails after the fact. So the גמרא needs a reason why this שופר is worse.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the second half of רב יהודה's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is one not יצא with a שופר of an עיר הנדחת, even though one is יצא with a שופר of עבודה זרה?

steps.title: The condemned city's property counts as already crushed
steps.stepSummary: Property of an עיר הנדחת must be burned, so the הלכה treats it as if it is already crushed to bits. The שופר is missing its required size.
steps.simpleTranslation: Things in an עיר הנדחת are treated as already crushed, so their size is gone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the שופר of an עיר הנדחת is treated as already destroyed, so it is not a proper-sized שופר at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem here is not about benefit. Since the תורה requires that everything in the city be burned, the הלכה sees it as already crushed, so the שופר does not have the minimum size a שופר needs. That is why even after the fact the person is not יצא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is considered crushed (as if already ground to bits)
The minimum size needed for a מצוה

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a problem that is not about benefit at all. Because the object must be burned, the הלכה treats it as if it lacks the required size, so the מצוה cannot be done with it even after the fact.

phrases.english: A city led astray:
its size is considered crushed.
phrases.notes: Since it is going to be burned anyway, the הלכה treats it as if it is already gone, so the שופר is too small to count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An עיר הנדחת is going to be burned, so its property is treated as already crushed and the שופר lacks the minimum size.

steps.title: A vow against benefit does not block blowing for a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that someone under a vow not to benefit from a person may still have that person blow שופר for him. Someone under a vow not to benefit from a שופר may still blow it for the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If someone is forbidden by a vow to benefit from his friend, the friend may still blow a מצוה blast for him. If someone is forbidden by a vow to benefit from a שופר, he may still blow a מצוה blast with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא applies his rule that a מצוה is not personal benefit to people who made a vow not to benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדר against benefit forbids any pleasure or gain. Since doing a מצוה does not count as benefit, hearing a friend's blast or blowing a forbidden שופר does not break the vow. This follows directly from רבא's conclusion in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who is forbidden by a vow to get benefit
A שופר blast done for the מצוה

phrases.english: Rava said:
One who is forbidden by vow to benefit from his friend:

phrases.aramaic: מוּתָּר לִתְקוֹעַ לוֹ תְּקִיעָה שֶׁל מִצְוָה.
phrases.english: the friend is permitted to blow a מצוה blast for him.
One who is forbidden by vow to benefit from a shofar:

phrases.aramaic: מוּתָּר לִתְקוֹעַ בּוֹ תְּקִיעָה שֶׁל מִצְוָה.
phrases.english: he is permitted to blow a מצוה blast with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבא's principle from step 16 to vows against benefit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow against benefit does not stop a מצוה blast, because doing a מצוה is not personal benefit.

steps.title: Sprinkling and immersion are allowed only when there is no pleasure
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a person under a vow may be sprinkled with מי חטאת, or immerse in a forbidden spring, in the rainy season but not in the hot season.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא also said: If someone is forbidden by vow to benefit from his friend, the friend may sprinkle purifying water on him in the rainy season, but not in the hot season. If someone is forbidden by vow to benefit from a spring, he may immerse in it for a מצוה in the rainy season, but not in the hot season.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to his rule: a מצוה is allowed only if it doesn't also give real physical pleasure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the rainy season, cold water gives no pleasure, so the sprinkling or immersion is only a מצוה. In the hot season, the water also cools the person off, which is real benefit, so it is forbidden. The principle that a מצוה is not benefit covers only the מצוה itself, not extra enjoyment that comes with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Purifying water mixed with the ashes of the פרה אדומה
Immersion in a spring or מקוה

steps.whatToRemember: A מצוה is not counted as benefit, but if the מצוה also gives physical pleasure (like cool water in summer), that pleasure is still forbidden.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
One who is forbidden by vow to benefit from his friend:

phrases.aramaic: מַזֶּה עָלָיו מֵי חַטָּאת בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים,
phrases.english: the friend may sprinkle purifying water on him in the rainy season,
but not in the hot season.
One who is forbidden by vow to benefit from a spring:
may immerse in it for a מצוה immersion
in the rainy season,
but not in the hot season.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הַמּוּדָּר הֲנָאָה מֵחֲבֵירוֹ מַזֶּה עָלָיו מֵי חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to step 20: the מצוה is allowed only when it gives no extra physical pleasure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sprinkling or immersion for a מצוה is allowed for someone under a vow against benefit in the rainy season, but not in the hot season when the water gives pleasure.

steps.title: A ruling sent: forced to eat מצה, he is יצא
steps.stepSummary: A ruling was sent to אבוה דשמואל: if someone was forced to eat מצה, he is יצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent a message to שמואל's father: If someone forced him and he ate מצה, he fulfilled the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling: a person who ate מצה because he was forced still fulfilled the מצוה. This opens a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This seems to say that a person can be יצא even without wanting to do the מצוה. The גמרא will now try to figure out what kind of forcing is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent to him (a ruling sent by message)

phrases.english: They sent to Shmuel's father:
If he was forced and ate מצה, he fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ לַאֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל: כְּפָאוֹ וְאָכַל מַצָּה יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about doing a מצוה without wanting to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who was forced to eat מצה is יצא.

steps.title: Who forced him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who did the forcing in this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who forced him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of forcing the ruling is talking about. This sets up the possibilities it will now test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling depends on what case it means. The גמרא will try one possibility and see if it holds up.

phrases.english: Who forced him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what case step 22 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of forcing is meant in the ruling about eating מצה?

steps.title: It can't mean a שד, since an insane person is exempt
steps.stepSummary: If a שד (a fit of insanity) made him eat, there is a problem: a ברייתא teaches that while a person is insane, he is treated as a שוטה in every way, so he would not be יצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say a שד forced him, there is a problem. A ברייתא teaches: someone who is sometimes sane and sometimes insane is treated as fully sane when he is sane, and as fully insane when he is insane.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the idea that a שד forced him and immediately challenges it with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'forced by a שד' means he ate during a fit of insanity. The ברייתא says that during such a time he counts as a שוטה, who is exempt from מצוות, so eating then could not make him יצא. The answer to who forced him must be something else, and the גמרא will continue looking.

keyTerms.meaning: A demon; here, a fit of insanity
An insane person, who is exempt from מצוות

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying a שד can't force someone. It is saying that a person who ate while insane counts as a שוטה, so he cannot be יצא.

phrases.english: If you say a demon forced him,
phrases.notes: He means the person ate during a fit of insanity.

phrases.english: but isn't it taught:
one who is sometimes sane and sometimes insane,

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁהוּא חָלִים — הֲרֵי הוּא כְּפִקֵּחַ לְכׇל דְּבָרָיו,
phrases.english: when he is sane, he is like a sane person in every way,

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁהוּא שׁוֹטֶה — הֲרֵי הוּא כְּשׁוֹטֶה לְכׇל דְּבָרָיו!
phrases.english: and when he is insane, he is like an insane person in every way!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one possible answer to step 23 and rejects it with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that 'forced' in the ruling means forced by a שד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person in a fit of insanity counts as a שוטה, who is exempt from מצוות. So eating מצה then cannot make him יצא, which contradicts the ruling.

steps.title: רב אשי: Persians forced him to eat
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the person was forced by Persians, not by a fit of insanity, so he was sane while eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is talking about a case where Persians forced him to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from the last step. The forcing was done by people (Persians), not by a שד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קשיא was that an insane person counts as a שוטה and cannot be יצא. רב אשי avoids this by saying the man was perfectly sane and was simply forced by others. So he really ate מצה as a normal person; he just did not mean to do the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Persians (here, people who force him by violence)

steps.whyThisMatters: Now the case is clean: a sane person did the act without meaning to do the מצוה. That is exactly what lets רבא learn a rule about intention in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Where Persians forced him.
phrases.notes: He means the man was sane. Other people made him eat, so the problem of being a שוטה from step 24 is gone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 24 by changing who did the forcing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (the forcing was by people, not by a שד)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The forcing was a fit of insanity, so the eater would be a שוטה and not יצא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Persians forced him while he was sane, so he is יצא even without meaning to do the מצוה.

steps.title: רבא: Blowing שופר for music still counts
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the forced-מצה ruling that a person who blows שופר just for music is יצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This teaches that one who blows the שופר for music is יצא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws a new rule from the מצה ruling. If you can be יצא with מצה without meaning to, the same is true for שופר blown only as music.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forced eater did not mean to do the מצוה, yet he was יצא. So רבא learns that doing a מצוה does not need intention. He applies this to someone who blows שופר only to make music: he is יצא too.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches / from this we learn
For music / to play a tune

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the start of the famous question of whether a מצוה needs intention (מצוות צריכות כוונה). רבא's view here is that it does not.
steps.confusionAlert: Being יצא with מצה is not just 'he ate food.' The point is that he did the מצוה act without meaning to do a מצוה, and רבא says that is enough.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is to say:
One who blows for music has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the now-clarified case from step 25 to draw a general rule about intention.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who blows שופר for music, with no thought of the מצוה, is יצא.

steps.title: Isn't this the same as the מצה case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say this, since it seems to be exactly the same as the מצה ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious! This is the same as that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that רבא's shofar rule adds nothing new. It is the same idea as the forced-מצה ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being יצא without intention works for מצה, why spell it out for שופר? A פשיטא question attacks a statement for being too obvious to need saying.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (so why say it?)
This is the same as that

phrases.english: It is obvious, this is the same as that!
phrases.notes: "That" is the forced-מצה ruling from step 22.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's statement in step 26 as being redundant.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that one who blows for music is יצא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is identical to the מצה ruling, so it teaches nothing new.

steps.title: Why שופר might have seemed different: the תורה said 'eat,' and he ate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining why you might have thought שופר is different: with מצה, the תורה only commands eating, and he did eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: There, the Merciful One said 'Eat מצה,' and he did eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer to the 'it's obvious' question. This is a setup line, and the full answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer suggests that מצה might be a special case. The תורה's command is simply to eat, and the eating really happened, so maybe that is why intention did not matter there. The next amud will show why שופר might have seemed different.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (an introduction to the mistaken idea)

phrases.english: Lest you say:
There, the Merciful One said: Eat matza —
and he did eat,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the פשיטא challenge of step 27 by suggesting a difference between מצה and שופר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a possible difference (a 'you might have thought'), which makes רבא's statement necessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מצה works without intention only because the Torah's command is simply 'eat,' and he ate.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not finished yet; the answer continues on the next amud.
